one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window, both on 2026-10-15: Alcoa's Q3 2026 results and call (after the close), and South32's shareholder vote on selling its aluminium assets to Alcoa. Q3 will be weaker than Q2's record $901M adjusted EBITDA. LME fell from about $3,800 at the peak to about $3,200-3,280, and the Midwest premium slipped to about 95c/lb. Management guided only small sequential items (alumina +$10M, tariff costs -$10M). The stock has already fallen about 50% from its June high of $84.38 and about 19% since early September, so I expect much of the weak quarter is priced in. The vote is likely to pass, since the independent expert called the deal fair and reasonable and the board backs it, so it should move the stock little. Q4 commentary and the alumina recovery at Pinjarra decide the direction, and I do not have a strong edge on them. On momentum versus reversal after the sharp drop, I lean only slightly toward reversal. So I used a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $42.2 with a 16% monthly sigma (56% annual / 3.5), widened a little for the earnings event.

fair_value.method: I blended mid-cycle EV/EBITDA (5x on a normalized $2.4B standalone EBITDA at about $3,000/t LME, giving ~$40) with forward P/E (11x on 2027E EPS of $3.9, giving ~$43) and a historical base-rate anchor (median 12-month price ratio about 1.0 after deep drawdowns, giving ~$45). The South32 deal (EV $4.7-5.6B, 17.0M new shares, closing H1 2027) is treated as roughly value-neutral.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Normalized 2027 standalone adj. EBITDA $2.4B x 5.0x = EV $12.0B; less net debt ~$0.8B and pension/other ~$0.6B gives equity ~$10.6B; / 266M diluted shares = ~$40. South32 assets taken as neutral (about $0.7B EBITDA at 5x ~ $3.5B vs ~$4.1B upfront + ~$0.75B assumed debt, offset by ~$900M NPV synergies).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 run-rate $3.6B was earned at a realized aluminium price of $4,752/t (LME ~$3,600+ plus a ~$1.09/lb Midwest premium). LME is now ~$3,280 and consensus 2027 views (Goldman ~$2,800-2,950, HLIB surplus) point to ~$3,000. The premium is down to ~95c/lb. At about -$200M annual EBITDA per -$100/t LME on 2.6-2.8Mt shipments, plus the lower premium, partly offset by Pinjarra recovering and restarted smelters, I get ~$2.4B.

Commodity producer near the cycle's upper-middle with a 2027 surplus risk. The stock's history (troughs ~4x, peaks ~6-7x forward) and the current ~8.6x TTM P/E at ~$11B market cap support a mid-cycle 5x.
The $2.6B of notes issued in September 2026 are pre-funding for the South32 cash consideration and are excluded from standalone net debt.

inputs_detail.value: $3.1B cash + 17.0M shares (~$1.0B) + CVR up to $750M; EV $4.7-5.6B; ~$900M NPV synergies; close H1 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM EPS is ~$4.9 (P/E 8.6 at $42). Q2 adj. EPS was $2.12 at peak prices. Scaling normalized EBITDA ($2.4B) less D&A ~$0.65B, interest ~$0.25B and ~30% tax gives ~$1.05B net / 270M shares, about $3.9.
Cyclical metals usually trade at 9-13x mid-cycle earnings. The current 8.6x on above-cycle TTM earnings suggests the market discounts lower forward earnings.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Base rate: AA monthly closes 2016-2026 give a median 12-month price ratio of ~1.0 (sd of log return ~0.64). After drawdowns >38% from the 6-month high, the forward 12-month ratio had a median of ~1.07 (wide range 0.6x-5x). Applied to $42, this gives ~$45.

inputs_detail.input: Historical 12m return distribution after deep drawdowns
inputs_detail.derivation: Computed from Twelve Data monthly closes June 2016 to Sept 2026, conditioning on close <62% of the trailing 6-month max close (15 instances, clustered in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2025).

bear.story: Hormuz normalizes and Gulf smelters restart, while Indonesian and Indian supply flips 2027 into a 1.5-2Mt surplus. LME falls to ~$2,600-2,800 and a US-Canada deal halves the 232 tariff, compressing the Midwest premium. Alcoa closes South32 with higher leverage at a worse point in the cycle, and the stock revisits 2025 levels (~$25-30).

base.story: LME is ~$2,900-3,200 and the premium stays elevated, since the US still imports ~4Mt and Canada can supply only ~3Mt. Pinjarra stabilizes and the South32 deal closes in H1 2027, accretive as guided. EBITDA is ~$2.4-2.8B at about 5x, which puts the stock in the low-to-mid $40s.

bull.story: Hormuz stays restricted into 2027 (Polymarket gives only ~20% to normal traffic by Dec 31, 2026), Gulf restarts are slow and the deficit persists. LME goes back above $3,600 with the premium near $1/lb, and South32 adds alumina/aluminium leverage plus ~$900M of synergies. The stock retraces toward the H1 2026 range of $60-80.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$29 (the post-tariff 2025 trading range, ~30% below today), the market would be pricing LME well under $2,800 and/or a failed or overpriced South32 integration with stressed leverage. That would mean the fundamentals broke, not ordinary 56%-vol noise around a $42 stock.

reasoning: Alcoa ran from ~$32 (Sep 2025) to $84.38 (Jun 2026) on the Middle East war: the near-closure of Hormuz cut Gulf aluminium supply and lifted LME to ~$3,800, while Section 232 tariffs pushed the Midwest premium to records. It then halved. Peace-talk hopes took LME to ~$3,200. Alcoa warned of an alumina loss from energy costs and Pinjarra problems. It also announced a $4.1B leveraged acquisition of South32's aluminium assets (stock fell 5%), and the Midwest premium dropped when the US-Canada tariff cut was floated. Q2 was still a record ($901M adj. EBITDA, $2.12 adj. EPS), so at $42 (~8.6x TTM P/E, ~$11B cap) the market is discounting a cyclical earnings decline. That fits the 2027 surplus forecasts. My normalized valuation (EV/EBITDA $40, P/E $43, base-rate $45) blends to ~$43, close to the current price. The consensus target of ~$60 looks stale relative to the commodity tape. Base rates: across 2016-2026, AA's 12-month log-return sd is ~0.64 (~0.5 excluding 2020-21) with median ratio ~1.0. Past >38% drawdowns (2018, 2022, 2025) produced both further 25-40% declines (2018, 2022) and multi-baggers (2020, 2025), so the outcome is close to symmetric in log space with fat tails. Prediction markets show Hormuz is still mostly closed (Polymarket: ~20% normal by Dec 31, ~11% by Nov 30), which supports near-term prices but leaves a downside step when it reopens. I used a lognormal with median ~$43 and sigma 0.50 (between realized 56% and a cooler forward view), with a slightly fatter left tail at the deep strikes. Research was limited to ~12 queries; the Bloomberg pages were blocked (403), so I relied on secondary summaries for the tariff story.
